english.title: Knowingly cause / permit use of trap to kill / take / restrain a Schedule 6 or Schedule 6ZA wild animal - Wales
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly caused or permitted use of any trap in Wales other than a glue trap for the purpose of killing, taking or restraining a wild animal included in Schedule 6 or Schedule 6ZA to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(2)(a)(ii), 11(2)(f) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) From the 17th October 2023, section 48 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 amends section 11 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981. This offence applies in Wales. For the offence applying in Wales and England before this date, see H20038.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(v) See section 11(7) for defence.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant knowingly caused or permitted use of any trap in Wales other than a glue trap for the purpose of killing, taking or restraining a wild animal included in Schedule 6 or Schedule 6ZA to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
